quote: Your 1.5T non-Si ECU has a built-in artificial rise in knock control anytime you go above 5200 rpm.
author: gtman

claim: After a fresh flash K.Con reads 0.6-0.7 and learns down to 0.49-0.56 by driving gently in a high gear (5th/6th about 40-50 mph); 0.49 is effectively zero
quote: On our cars "0" knock control is around 49%-51%, it will never go lower.
author: multiple incl KTuner

claim: Stock calibration showed K.Con 0.9 and KTuner said that was normal for factory; FlashPro-style tuners see high 50s on race tunes; aggressive timing raises K.Con which then pulls timing
quote: When I had the stock calibrations on the car the knock control was at .9 and Ktuner said that was normal for factory.
author: multiple incl KTuner

claim: KTuner staff: knock control system is always active on factory or flash tune; data points exist regardless of whether you monitor them
quote: The knock control system is always active and adjusting.
author: multiple incl KTuner

claim: Tuner view: if K.Con climbs on every pull the ECU is detecting knock and tune timing is too aggressive for the 91 octane; CA 91 factory timing is on the edge
quote: If knock control climbs each time you make a pull, then the ECU is detecting some sort of knock condition.
author: multiple incl KTuner

claim: Starter 21 default final target 22.5 psi; six targets exist (3 ECO and 3 Normal) editable individually; Boost By Gear limits the target tables, so if the target is lower than BBG the target table is used
quote: BBG limits the target tables, so if the target is lower than BBG it will just run the targets from the target table.
author: KTuner staff
ktuner_table_or_setting: Boost Target 1-3 Eco/Normal / Boost by gear

claim: Table editing in KTuner software: direct entry, Ctrl-J, or Ctrl up/down; dial back lower-rpm cells to keep a smooth 3D curve
quote: Adjusting the table can be done by direct entry, control-J, or control up/down.
author: KTuner staff

claim: Example BBG set by 6MT owner: 1st 12, 2nd 14, 3rd 18, 4th 20, 5th 21 psi (6th disabled)
quote: 1ST= 12PSI 2ND = 14PSI 3RD= 18PSI 4TH=20PSI 5TH=21PSI
author: KTuner staff

claim: Ideal K.Con is 0.49 on KTuner and 0.54 on Hondata; over 1 is concerning but not proof of mechanical issue; hot weather, steep hills and low octane raise it; bad gas after multiple pulls can reach 1
quote: Ideal on KTuner is .49 and .54 on Hondata.
author: gtman

claim: Fine-tuning MAF scale across eight tunes moved K.Con floor from 0.49 to 0.64-0.70; flashing back to stock returned 0.49 (MAF changes can raise K.Con)
quote: Now its lowest is .64 and could go up to .70.
author: gtman

claim: 0.59 is the K.Con starting point right after flashing a KTuner tune; then learns down; K.Con about 0.1-0.15 higher climbing a hill in 100F+ heat
quote: FYI .59 is the exact starting point when you flash a KTuner tune onto these ECUs.
author: multiple

claim: Owner on 91 octane: K.Con stays 0.49 in normal driving but reaches 0.72 after hard pulls over 5500 rpm; on 94 never exceeded 0.54
quote: if I drive it real hard and go over 5500 rpms a couple times it'll go up to .72
author: multiple

claim: On E40 blend K.Con consistently 0.49-0.51
quote: E40 blend, and I'm consistently at .49 to .51
author: multiple

claim: Typical overshoot is 1-2 psi (22.8 psi peak on 21 psi target); a 24 psi spike on 17 target was a logging glitch since target channel jumped to -3.9 in the same sample
quote: Since the target suddenly jumps to -3.9, which isn't accurate, I suggest that's a glitch.
author: KTuner staff / gtman

claim: Boost misbehavior case: MAP spiking to 27 psi with K.Con 1.3-1.05 and slow boost build then overshoot; KTuner: wastegate controls boost and a pressure leak (coupler, O-ring after intercooler install) can cause compensation
quote: The wastegate is what controls boost pressure. You could also have a pressure leak
author: KTuner staff / gtman

claim: 1.5R Non-Si map 3 peaks at 24 psi and TSP 1 around 23.5 psi; self-tuning boost without timing and fueling is the recipe for a blown hatch rod
quote: Map 3 of the 1.5R Non-Si tune peaks at 24. TSP 1 at around 23.5 psi.
author: gtman

claim: European 5AN-EKx ECU cars show TPS.CMD never reaching 100 percent (95 percent at WOT) and boost target 18-19 psi instead of 21; seen on a few non-North American cars
quote: at wot it is always 95%
author: gtman

claim: KTuner: Civic tunes are outlined with specific boost levels but Accord tunes are not; target in table does not guarantee boost, ECU adjusts to environment; boost target is not the only change in the tune
quote: No, that does not mean the machine must reach it.
author: KTuner staff

claim: KTuner software tables named in thread: Ignition base, Ignition Maximum (with EGR), Knock sensitivity, WOT enrichment (MGStk), Boost target / final boost target (TB), Cylinder fill limitation (K.Ret); official explanations are on KTuner Help table of contents
quote: WOT enrichment, how do we compare or relate MGStk with the MAF values in datalogs
author: multiple
ktuner_table_or_setting: WOT enrichment / Cylinder fill limitation / Ignition maximum / Knock sensitivity

claim: Self-tuning warning: one engine failure in the reliability thread was caused by self tuning; a single bad adjustment can cause serious damage
quote: Self tuning has caused at least one engine failure in my thread.
author: multiple

claim: With PRL Cobra race MAF plus TSP Stage 1 race-MAF tune: LTFT about +4.5 percent to -6.25 percent and STFT +7 to -11 percent judged normal; short-term trims fluctuate by design and LTFT is the number that matters
quote: Short term trims are meant to fluctuate and sometimes wildly
author: gtman

claim: TSP Stage 1 K.Con shot to .94 by 80 mph on one pull from 20 mph (.7x at 60-65 mph); Phearable 1.5R Non-Si race tune removes the artificial K.Con rise, base Phearable 1.5 and TSP do not; artificial rise exists only on non-Si tunes
quote: only the Non-Si R tune removes that, not the base 1.5 tune
author: gtman

claim: KTuner base tune lets you manually choose the remove-artificial-knock option
quote: I tested the Ktuner base tune and was able to manually choose the 'remove artificial knock' option.
author: gtman

claim: Staged tunes are older and mostly locked; Starter tunes allow throttle and turbo adjustments and arbitrary boost levels (even below stock); Stage 2 (21 psi) works on a stock car on high octane; factory about 15 psi
quote: Stage 2 is 21 psi. You can run Stg2 on an otherwise bone stock car
author: gtman

claim: 87 octane works on base tunes but gives elevated knock control which reduces timing and power; KTuner base tunes are fairly conservative
quote: You can use 87 but you'll have elevated knock control which reduces timing which in turn lowers power output.
author: gtman

claim: Example conservative 21 psi starter quick adjustments: improved turbo responsiveness II and ramp II; another: throttle response II, turbo spool II, eco normalized, responsiveness II
quote: improved turbo responsiveness II and ramp up II
author: gtman
